lemma: L1 (time-invariant unrolling, exact). Let C be a circuit with s gates, inputs x in {0,1}^n, depth d(g) = 1 + max d(inputs of g) (inputs have depth 0), output gate o, D = max_g d(g). Define the time-invariant system with state sigma in {0,1}^s, sigma^0 = 0, and update sigma^{t}_g = op_g(val_a, val_b) where val reads x_i or sigma^{t-1}_h. Claim: for all t and all g with d(g) <= t, sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Proof by induction on t: t=0 vacuous (no gate has depth 0). Step t-1 -> t: a gate g with d(g) <= t has every input h with d(h) <= t-1, so sigma^{t-1}_h = C_h(x) by hypothesis, hence sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Corollary: sigma^D_o = C(x) after D steps, with D*s gate evaluations in total. L1' (time-dependent schedule, exact): at step t evaluate exactly the gates with d(g) = t; each gate is evaluated once, so s evaluations in total and the output is correct after D steps. Consequence: the two cost accountings differ by a factor D for uniform (time-invariant) updates, and agree for depth-scheduled updates.

lemma: L2 (cost accounting, exact). For a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates and depth D (D <= s): the time-invariant uniform system (L1) costs D*s gate evaluations in total with update width s per step; the depth-scheduled system (L1') costs s in total with per-step width W_t = number of gates at depth t, and max_t W_t <= s. Hence the time-invariant overhead in total work is exactly the factor D, with 1 <= D <= s, so the two accountings differ by at most a polynomial factor s. The worst case W = s is attained, so the per-step width gives no saving in general. Dispute K9-D4 reading: Position Claude (zero overhead) is exact for time-dependent depth schedules; Position ChatGPT (cost can differ) is exact for time-invariant uniform updates, with overhead factor D, polynomial in s. Both are correct under their own accounting; the disagreement is which update cost U is meant. Status: CLAIMED, bookkeeping, needs independent review.

lemma: L3 (time-invariant worklist, exact). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates whose gate indices are topological (each gate input is an input bit or a gate with smaller index). The system has state: value bits val[g], in-degree counters ind[g] (initially the number of gate inputs of g, counted with multiplicity), and a queue Q (initially all gates with ind = 0). Each step pops one gate g from Q, computes val[g] from its two inputs (input bits or already-computed values), and for each successor k of g decrements ind[k] and pushes k when ind[k] reaches 0. The step rule is the same at every step. Claim: the run performs exactly s pops and val equals C at all gates. Proof: (i) each gate is pushed exactly once, because ind[k] reaches 0 exactly once; (ii) a gate is pushed only after all its gate inputs are popped, so its inputs are already computed when it is popped; (iii) every gate reaches ind = 0, by induction on index, because its inputs have smaller index and so are eventually popped. Hence s pops, each gate computed once from correct inputs. Cost: s gate evaluations; state O(s log s) bits; update O(1) amortised per pop. Consequence for K9-D4: the factor D overhead of L1 is removed, but only by enlarging the state beyond s value bits and by random access to the static gate description. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review.

proved_step: L4 (stream order, exact, bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, and let pi list its gates once each. Consider the one-pass rule: on arrival, compute the gate from its two inputs read from value memory, with s value bits and no other state. This rule computes C correctly in s steps if and only if pi is a topological order of the gate DAG. Proof: if pi is topological, induction on position shows every arriving gate's inputs are already stored, so each value is correct and exactly s steps are used. If pi is not topological, some gate g arrives before one of its gate inputs h; when g arrives the slot of h is still empty, so the rule reads an undefined value. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. This is bookkeeping and closes no obligation.

proved_step: L5 (arbitrary labelling, exact bookkeeping). Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, labelled in any order. Rule: at each step, among the gates not yet computed whose gate inputs are all computed (inputs of the circuit count as computed), compute the one with the smallest label. Claim: the rule is never stuck, performs exactly s steps, and every computed value equals C at that gate. Proof: let D(g) be the longest path from an input to g, so D(g) is at least 1 for gates and every gate input of g has smaller D. Suppose some gate is uncomputed at a point where the rule is stuck, and pick an uncomputed gate g of minimum D. Its gate inputs have smaller D, so they are computed, so g is ready, a contradiction. Hence the rule runs until all s gates are computed. Each step evaluates one gate whose inputs already hold correct values, so each value is correct by induction on the step count. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. Bookkeeping: it closes no obligation and does not by itself settle K9-D4.

refuted_approach: L4 'only if' direction (a one-pass rule with s value bits computes C correctly iff the stream order is topological) is FALSE as stated. Counterexample: one input x; gates h = AND(x,x) = x and g = OR(h,x) = x; order (g,h) is not topological; with initial slot value 0, g = 0 OR x = x (correct), then h = x, so both outputs are correct for every x. The rule has no undefined marker: an unfilled slot holds an arbitrary bit. With initial value 1, g = 1 OR x is wrong at x = 0, so the outcome depends on the initial state. Surviving statement: if the order is topological, the rule is correct in s steps (L4 'if' direction, CLAIMED, needs review). A converse must quantify over circuits, or fix the initial state and require correctness for all circuits.

Synchronous D-round update (all gates recomputed from the previous round's values, starting from 0) gives the correct value at every gate in 1050/1050 circuits. Prefix invariant 'depth(g) <= t implies val_t(g) = C(g)' holds in 1050/1050. Argument check: induction on t. A gate of depth t has gate inputs of depth at most t-1, which are correct after round t-1 by hypothesis, so its round-t value is correct. Base case t=0 holds because depth-0 gates have only input-bit inputs. No gap found; the lab run is a finite agreement only. proved_step: LEMMA (ready-set scan cost, exact bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates. Run the smallest-label rule of S0006 and count readiness tests, where one test checks whether a gate's two gate inputs are computed. Claim: the rule performs exactly s steps, each step performs at most s readiness tests, so the total is at most s^2 tests and at most 2 s^2 input-slot reads. Proof: S0006 gives exactly s steps. At step t the rule tests each not-yet-computed gate at most once, and at most s gates exist, so at most s tests per step. Summing over s steps gives at most s^2 tests. Each test reads at most two input slots, giving at most 2 s^2 reads. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review.

proved_step: LEMMA (store-then-run one-pass rule, CLAIMED). Model: a fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates is presented as a stream of s records (g, op_g, in_g1, in_g2), in an arbitrary order (a permutation of gate labels), each record read once; inputs x are available by random access. Algorithm: (1) during the single pass, write each record into a table T indexed by g; each record costs O(1) update; (2) after the pass, run the L3 worklist on T with no further reads of the stream. Claim: the run returns val[g] = C(x)_g for every gate, performs exactly s pops and s pushes, and E <= 2s decrements, where E is the number of gate-to-gate edges. Proof: after the pass T is exactly the description of C under the relabelling g, so T is a fan-in-2 DAG description of C. L3's proof (i)-(iii) uses only that every gate-input edge is counted in ind, and that C is acyclic (so (iii) induction on a topological order exists); both hold. Hence the run is correct, with s pops and s pushes by L3. Cost: state O(s log s) bits (value bits plus indices and op codes per record); update O(1) per record; post-pass O(s + E) = O(s) operations with random access into T.
